title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Self-radicalised Singaporeans under ISA
sections.summary: ISD says at least eight self-radicalised Singaporeans were dealt with under the ISA between July 2024 and July 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to the Internal Security Department (ISD), between July 2024 and July 2025, at least eight self-radicalised Singaporeans were dealt with under the Internal Security Act (ISA).

sections.label: Youths dealt with under ISA
sections.summary: ISD reports 17 youths aged 20 and below dealt with under the ISA since 2015, with nine intending local attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The ISD has reported that 17 youths aged 20 and below have been dealt with under the ISA since 2015, with more than two-thirds in the last five years; nine intended to mount local attacks, with three in 2025 alone.

sections.label: Phishing attempts reported to CSA
sections.summary: Phishing attempts reported to the CSA rose from 4,100 in 2023 to 6,100 in 2024, a 49% increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, phishing attempts reported to the CSA increased from 4,100 in 2023 to 6,100 in 2024, an increase of 49%.

sections.label: Drug abusers arrested statistics
sections.summary: CNB annual statistics show drug abusers arrested rose modestly from 3,175 in 2024 to 3,208 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Central Narcotics Bureau's (CNB's) latest annual statistics show that the number of drug abusers arrested increased modestly from 3,175 in 2024 to 3,208 in 2025.

sections.label: Scam and cybercrime losses
sections.summary: Losses to scams and cybercrime rose to at least $1.1 billion in 2024, with measures proposed to address the threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Statistics show that in 2024, the total amount lost to scams and cybercrime rose to at least $1.1 billion, up from $651.8 million in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2025, the amount lost was about $456.4 million, a 12.6% decrease from the year before but still a significant figure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, Government official impersonation scams in the first half of 2025 almost tripled to 1,762 cases, with the amounts lost to this type of scam increasing by about 89% to $126.5 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Scammers are increasingly sophisticated, leveraging AI-generated voices, deepfakes, spoofed numbers and social engineering tactics to create urgency and fear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We must harness technology to address the threat of scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This includes detecting suspicious transaction patterns in real time, strengthening digital forensics and cross-border intelligence cooperation to disrupt syndicates and embedding stronger safeguards in our banking and payment systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must continue to focus on public education and equip Singaporeans with the knowledge and tools to spot and respond to scam activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I also support the tough approach we are taking on those in Singapore who facilitate scams, including by opening bank accounts or setting up phone lines.

sections.label: Drug abuse and mental health data
sections.summary: A survey links drug abuse to mental health conditions, and the MP asks if data on arrestees' mental health will be collected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The 2024 Singapore Health and Lifestyle Survey demonstrates strong links between drug abuse and mental health conditions such as anxiety, depression and insomnia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Prison Service attributes recent improvements to evidence-informed throughcare drug rehabilitation regime with strong community support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We currently lack systematic data on the mental health profiles of those arrested for drug abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Minister, does the Ministry plan to collect data on the mental health status of individuals arrested for drug-related offences?

sections.label: Ex-offender reintegration and criminal records
sections.summary: MHA is asked about support for ex-offenders securing work and whether laws like the Registration of Criminals Act can be reviewed so records are spent earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can MHA share how far we have come in supporting ex-offenders in their reintegration journey, especially in helping them secure meaningful work and rebuild stable lives?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: And will the Ministry consider reviewing laws such as the Registration of Criminals Act, including whether some records can be spent earlier where appropriate so that those who have truly turned over a new leaf are not locked out of opportunity for life?

sections.label: Rise in five-year recidivism rate
sections.summary: Singapore Prison Service data shows the five-year recidivism rate rose from 36.6% for the 2019 cohort to 39.3% for the 2020 cohort, viewed in the pandemic context.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to the latest data from the Singapore Prison Service, the five-year recidivism rate rose, from 36.6% for the 2019 release cohort, to 39.3% for the 2020 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is reasonable to view this in the context of the pandemic, a period marked by economic uncertainty, hiring slowdowns and reduced face-to-face supervision and support services.

sections.label: Rehabilitation strategy targets and metrics
sections.summary: MHA is asked for medium-term quantitative targets for reducing five-year recidivism and whether it will publish a 2026 to 2030 rehabilitation strategy with an outcome matrix.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A forward-looking rehabilitation framework with clear outcome metrics such as employment retention, housing stability and community integration indicators would help sustain momentum and reinforce public confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Minister, what is MHA's medium-term quantitative targets for reducing five-year recidivism over the next five years?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will MHA publish a forward-looking 2026 to 2030 rehabilitation strategy with a clear outcome matrix, including employment, retention, housing stability and community integration indicators?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Three, how does MHA assess the effectiveness of current employer partnership schemes and other plans to expand structured post-placement support to reduce relapsed risk?

sections.label: FRONTIER+ asset recovery operations
sections.summary: Parliament was told the Police formalised FRONTIER+, and joint operations across six jurisdictions last year recovered more than $26 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Parliament was told in November that the Police had formalised the Funds Recovery Operations and Networks Team, Inspiring Effective Resolution Plus (FRONTIER+), an initiative among several jurisdictions, to strengthen real-time intelligence sharing, improve asset recovery and coordinate joint operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under FRONTIER+, joint operations had reportedly been conducted last year across six jurisdictions that led to the recovery of more than $26 million.

sections.label: Scam losses total
sections.summary: Scam losses still totalled a significant $456 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Scam losses still totalled a significant $456 million.

sections.label: Meta revenue from scam ads
sections.summary: Reuters reported Meta platforms were expected to earn US$16 billion, or 10% of its 2024 revenue, from ads for scams or other illicit products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, Reuters reported in November last year that Meta platforms, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp were expected to earn US$16 billion or 10% of its revenue in 2024 from ads for scams or other illicit products.

sections.label: VCO activation in scam cases
sections.summary: The passage asks in what percentage of scam cases VCOs have been activated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In what percentage of scam cases have VCOs been activated?

sections.label: Government-private sector anti-scam plans
sections.summary: The passage asks what plans the Government has to work with the private sector to fight scams more effectively.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What are the plans that the Government have to work with the private sector to fight scams more effectively?

sections.label: Scam laws and falling case numbers
sections.summary: Parliament enacted laws empowering authorities against scams, and scam cases fell from over 50,000 in 2024 to 37,308 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the last few years, Parliament has enacted the Online Criminal Harms Act, the Law Enforcement and Other Matters Act and the Protection from Scams Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These laws have empowered the authorities to, amongst other things, issue directions to online platforms requiring action against fraudulent accounts or content; criminalise the misuse of SIM cards and the handing over of bank accounts or Singpass credentials to be misused by others; and facilitate the issuance of Restriction Orders to freeze the bank accounts of victims, thereby delaying the siphoning away of funds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have even introduced mandatory caning for serious scam offences, syndicate members and recruiters, by passing the Criminal Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And it is heartening to know that for the first time in eight years, the number of scam cases in Singapore has fallen from more than 50,000 in 2024 to 37,308 in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amount lost to scammers has also dipped below $1 billion although it is still a large amount.

sections.label: 2025 scam case and loss figures
sections.summary: In 2025 scam cases fell 27.6% and losses fell 17.9%, but 37,308 cases and $913.1 million lost remain concerning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in 2025, the number of scam cases decreased by 27.6% or 14,193 cases from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Importantly, losses from scams also fell by 17.9% or by $199.3 million in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, with 37,308 scam cases, totalling a loss of $913.1 million in 2025, the situation remains extremely concerning and combating scams must remain a top priority this year.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Command recoveries and interventions
sections.summary: In 2025 the Anti-Scam Command recovered $140.5 million and helped victims avert at least $348 million in potential losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In 2025, the Anti-Scam Command successfully recovered $140.5 million worth of scam losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Importantly, it is reported that through proactive interventions with victims in the various stages of being scammed, the Anti-Scam Command managed to work with its partners to help victims avert potential losses of at least $348 million.

sections.label: Dangerous driving death penalties concern
sections.summary: The passage raises concern that penalties for aggravated dangerous driving causing death may not reflect the harm caused.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: While our laws rightly distinguish between levels of culpability, there remains concern that certain aggravated cases of dangerous driving causing death may not be met with penalties that fully reflect the harm caused.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: One case that has been widely discussed is that of Jarrett Tee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The court dealt with the matter under the existing framework for dangerous driving causing death.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: However, the case has raised broader questions among members of the public as to whether the current range of penalties sufficiently capture conduct that, while falling short of intent to kill, nonetheless reflects a very high degree of recklessness and disregard for the safety of others.

sections.label: AI budget for operations
sections.summary: A $400 million budget was committed to embed AI into operations including emergency response, investigative work and a 500-strong AI workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A significant budget of $400 million was committed with the aim of embedding AI into operations from emergency response, investigative work and grooming a 500 strong AI workforce.

sections.label: Unattended cooking residential fires
sections.summary: Unattended cooking remains one of the leading causes of residential fires in Singapore, according to the SCDF.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Chairman, unattended cooking remains one of the leading causes of residential fires in Singapore, according to the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

sections.label: Hong Kong high-rise fire lessons
sections.summary: A Hong Kong fire burned 43 hours and 27 minutes, killing 168 people, prompting questions on lessons and high-rise fire safety technology.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 26 November 2025, a large fire broke out at the Wang Fuk Court apartment, Hong Kong, and burned for 43 hours and 27 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Seven out of the eight blocks of the complex were consumed by fire, and 168 people died, including one firefighter.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, high rise fires are really a big concern in urban cities and that is where we need to pay attention.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand SCDF has aerial appliances that can catch reach up to 90 metres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My question is, what lessons has MHA drawn from this tragic fire in Hong Kong?

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What are the new ways or new technologies for addressing high rise fire safety, especially for buildings that are 100 metres and above, or 20 storeys and higher.

sections.label: Zero tolerance towards drugs
sections.summary: Because reversals have a long tail that is not easily unwound, Singapore's stance must remain zero tolerance towards drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The reality is that reversals have a long tail, which is not easily unwound.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore's stance must continue to be one of zero tolerance towards drugs.

sections.label: Updating Misuse of Drugs Act
sections.summary: The Misuse of Drugs Act must be updated to maintain its deterrence against new drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In line with this, we must update the Misuse of Drugs Act to maintain its deterrence against new drugs.

sections.label: Drug stance and rehabilitation
sections.summary: The Misuse of Drugs Act requires political courage, and a muscular stance against traffickers does not contradict a commitment to rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Misuse of Drugs Act requires political courage because the buck ultimately stops with those elected – us, here – to make hard decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: At the same time, there is no contradiction in pairing this muscular stance against traffickers with a sincere commitment to rehabilitation.

sections.label: Deterrence and rehabilitation approach
sections.summary: The approach deters traffickers with muscle and rehabilitates those earnest in turning their lives around.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In this way, our approach remains principled and coherent – to deter traffickers with our muscle, and with our hearts, we rehabilitate those who are earnest in turning their lives around.

sections.label: Principle of political ambidexterity
sections.summary: Helping sincere addicts through rehabilitation, employment support and reintegration is right, and this principle of political ambidexterity should guide legislative work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: At the same time, helping addicts who are sincere in kicking the habit through rehabilitation, employment support and reintegration is the right thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This principle, which I coin the principle of political ambidexterity, should guide all our legislative work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: When debating Bills in this House and during Committee of Supply discussions, we must be willing to draw from different policy tools without being beholden to ideology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A rigid, purist approach, either entirely left leaning or entirely right leaning, risks missing the complexity of real-world problems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We should never be slaves to ideology, nor should we chase populism.

sections.label: New drug abusers arrested 2025
sections.summary: In 2025, 1,165 new drug abusers were arrested, a 17% rise, with one in two below 30 and the youngest 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2025, 1,165 new drug abusers were arrested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: That is a 17% increase from the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Even more troubling, one in two of these new abusers was below the age of 30, and the youngest person arrested was just 12 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Among those under 20, nearly 80% were abusing methamphetamine.

sections.label: CNB dismantled drug syndicates
sections.summary: CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates last year, including those operating through Telegram and from overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the same time, CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates last year, including those operating through Telegram and from overseas.

sections.label: Singapore safety rankings and confidence
sections.summary: Singapore was ranked the world's safest country in Gallup's 2025 report, and 94.9% of survey respondents had confidence in the Home Team.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In Gallup's 2025 Global Safety Report, Singapore was ranked the world's safest country for the 12th time – 98% of the respondents said they felt safe walking alone at night.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In a public perception survey conducted last year, 94.9% of the respondents had confidence in the Home Team's ability to keep Singapore safe and secure.

sections.label: Road fatalities and traffic violations
sections.summary: Road traffic fatalities hit a 10-year high since 2016, with speeding violations up 26% and red-light running incidents up 27%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Road traffic fatalities have hit a 10-year high since 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Speeding violations last year rose by 26% compared to 2024, and a 27% increase was observed for red-light running related incidents and accidents.

sections.label: ISD self-radicalised individuals
sections.summary: Since 2015, ISD has dealt with 62 self-radicalised individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since 2015, ISD has dealt with 62 self-radicalised individuals.

sections.label: Emergency preparedness familiarity rise
sections.summary: In 2025, 69% of Singaporeans said they were familiar with or trained in emergency preparedness skills, compared to 40% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2025, 69% of Singaporeans said that they were familiar with or have been trained in emergency preparedness skills, compared to 40% in 2017.

sections.label: Suspicious object social experiments
sections.summary: In social experiments last year, only 17% who walked past suspicious objects noticed anything amiss, and only 6% of them tried to inform authorities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In several social experiments conducted last year, only 17% of those who walked past suspicious objects noticed anything amiss, and even then, only 6% of them attempted to inform the authorities.

sections.label: RHA measures in force
sections.summary: The Ministry is planning to bring RHA, including these measures, into force by end-2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: My Ministry is planning to bring RHA, including these measures, into force by end-2026.

sections.label: Amend FICA anticipatory directions
sections.summary: The Government will amend FICA to propose allowing anticipatory directions against online communication mediums, including websites and mobile applications, before they cause actual harm.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will therefore amend FICA, so that our legislation can be more effective against such threats.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will propose to allow the Government to issue anticipatory directions against mediums of online communications, including websites and mobile applications, should there be indications that they may be used to mount an HIC against Singapore, before they cause actual harm.

sections.label: SCDF extends FC validity
sections.summary: Given industry compliance, the Singapore Civil Defence Force will extend the validity of FCs from one year to three years, effective 1 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Given this strong track record of industry compliance, the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) will extend the validity of FCs from one year to three years, effective from 1 April 2026.

sections.label: HDB senior HFAD subsidies
sections.summary: HDB's Enhancement for Active Seniors programme subsidises HFADs up to 95%, with public rental flat residents receiving them free.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Through the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) Enhancement for Active Seniors programme, we provide subsidies of up to 95% for HFADs, with seniors paying as little as $6 out of pocket.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Those staying in public rental flats, many of whom are elderly, are also provided HFADs for free.

sections.label: Differentiated EV licence plates study
sections.summary: MHA and MOT are studying differentiated licence plates for EVs, as done in other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MHA and the Ministry of Transport (MOT) are therefore studying the use of differentiated licence plates for EVs, as has been done in other countries.

sections.label: Non-compliant PMD possession offence
sections.summary: All recorded AMD fatalities involved PMDs not complying with UL-2272, and keeping such devices becomes an offence from 1 June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: All recorded AMD fatalities to date have involved personal mobility devices which did not comply with UL-2272 standards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: From 1 June 2026, keeping such non-compliant devices at home or anywhere else will be an offence.

sections.label: Methamphetamine seizures in East Southeast Asia
sections.summary: UNODC reported 236 tonnes of methamphetamine seized in East and Southeast Asia in 2024, a 24% rise from 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime reported that 236 tonnes of methamphetamine were seized in East and Southeast Asia in 2024, a 24% jump from 2023.

sections.label: CNB 2025 syndicates and seizures
sections.summary: In 2025, CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates and seized over $21 million worth of drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2025, CNB dismantled 25 drug syndicates and seized more than $21 million worth of drugs.

sections.label: CNB international joint operations
sections.summary: In 2025, CNB conducted 18 joint operations with international partners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2025, CNB conducted 18 joint operations with our international partners.

sections.label: Young new abusers arrested
sections.summary: In 2025, about half of newly arrested abusers were under age 30.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2025, about half of the new abusers arrested were below the age of 30.

sections.label: Support for drug laws
sections.summary: Most youth and adult respondents supported maintaining tough drug laws, and the Misuse of Drugs Act will be amended this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: There is also a strong support for Singapore's drug-related laws. 92.7% of the youth respondents and 96.3% of the adult respondents felt that we should continue to maintain our tough laws to keep drugs out of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will be amending the Misuse of Drugs Act this year to enhance investigative and enforcement levers against drug-related activities.

sections.label: Supervision 2.0 implementation
sections.summary: Following the pilot's success, Supervision 2.0 was fully implemented in May 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Given the pilot's success, we fully implemented Supervision 2.0 in May 2025.

sections.label: DRC release cohort recidivism
sections.summary: The two-year recidivism rate for the 2023 Drug Rehabilitation Centre release cohort fell 4.7 percentage points to 26.1%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The two-year recidivism rate for the 2023 Drug Rehabilitation Centre's release cohort decreased by 4.7 percentage points to 26.1%, compared to the previous cohort.

sections.label: Overall population recidivism rate
sections.summary: The two-year recidivism rate for the overall population stayed low and stable at 21.9% for the 2023 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The two-year recidivism rate for the overall population remained low and stable, at 21.9% for the 2023 release cohort.

sections.label: Five-year overall recidivism rate
sections.summary: The five-year overall recidivism rate rose 2.7 percentage points to 39.3% for the 2020 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The five-year overall recidivism rate has increased by 2.7 percentage points to 39.3% for the 2020 release cohort.

sections.label: Skills training pathways for inmates
sections.summary: There will be more skills training pathways, including a pilot partnership with Temasek Polytechnic for inmates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Second, there will be more skills training pathways.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This includes a pilot partnership with Temasek Polytechnic to develop a programme that introduces SkillsFuture Singapore-accredited courses in Communications and Graphics, and Media and Content Creation for inmates.

sections.label: YRSG employment and employer support
sections.summary: YRSG ran coaching workshops, had over 6,400 supportive employers, and 94% of over 2,100 inmates secured jobs in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since 2024, YRSG has partnered with training academies to deliver five workplace coaching and mentoring workshops, training 71 supervisors from 23 partner employers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As at end 2025, there were more than 6,400 employers who support the hiring of ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: YRSG provided employment statistics to over 2,100 inmates, of which 94% secured jobs in 2025.

sections.label: Volunteer training spaces increase
sections.summary: SPS provided 2,200 volunteer training spaces in 2025, rising to 4,500 in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Under the Igniting and Maximising Partners' Agility for Correctional Transformation programme, SPS provided 2,200 training spaces in 2025 for our volunteers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2026, the number of training spaces will be increased to 4,500.

sections.label: Robot and emergency alert trials
sections.summary: Prisons will trial the PROTECT robot in FY2026, and SCDF will roll out SG Alert from May 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: At Singapore Prisons, we will be trialling the use of PROTECT, a robot designed to support officers during patrols and yard supervision, in the first quarter of FY2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: From May 2026, SCDF will progressively roll out SG Alert, which is a dedicated mass emergency alert system that can broadcast emergency alerts to mobile handsets islandwide or within specific geographical zones.

sections.label: Police reports via self-help
sections.summary: Over 70% of Police reports are now lodged through self-help services online or at kiosks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: With the Singapore Police Force's (SPF's) digitalisation efforts over the years, more than 70% of all Police reports are now lodged through self-help services, either online or at self-help kiosks located in Neighbourhood Police Centres (NPCs) and Neighbourhood Police Posts.

sections.label: HTX AI workforce and Phoenix
sections.summary: HTX's AI specialist workforce reached 250 by end-2025, and the Phoenix Large Language Model launched in May 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Home Team Science and Technology Agency's (HTX's) AI specialist workforce has grown to 250 as at end-2025 and is on track to reach 400 by end of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Another milestone was in May 2025 when we launched the first in a series of Home Team proprietary Large Language Models, codenamed Phoenix.

sections.label: AI governance testing platform
sections.summary: In 2026, HTX will develop a proof-of-concept for a centralised AI Governance Testing and Monitoring Platform to automate AI governance checks and ensure continuous compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2026, HTX will develop a proof-of-concept for a centralised AI Governance Testing and Monitoring Platform to automate AI governance checks and ensure continuous compliance throughout the AI lifecycle.

sections.label: Traffic violation enforcement camera trial
sections.summary: In 2025, a new Traffic Violation Enforcement Camera using video analytics and automatic number plate recognition was trialled to detect traffic violations in real time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2025, we trialled the new Traffic Violation Enforcement Camera, which leverages video analytics and automatic number plate recognition to detect and capture various traffic violations in real time.

sections.label: Rising traffic fatality rate
sections.summary: The traffic fatality rate has been rising, increasing by about 24% from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As shared in the Annual Road Traffic Situation released yesterday, our traffic fatality rate has been rising, increasing by about 24% from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: Lowering drink driving limit
sections.summary: The drink driving limit will be lowered to 15 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Evidence shows that impairment to driving skills occurs at lower levels of alcohol concentration and that crash risks increase with alcohol consumption.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will therefore lower the drink driving limit to 15 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath.

sections.label: Tightening demerit points system
sections.summary: MHA is considering tightening the Driver Improvement Points System, also known as the demerit points system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To motivate all drivers to adhere more closely to traffic rules, MHA is considering tightening the Driver Improvement Points System, otherwise more commonly known as the demerit points system.

sections.label: Road safety campaign and enforcement
sections.summary: A new publicity campaign on road safety will be launched, enforcement strengthened starting with drink-driving, the drink-driving limit lowered to 15 microgrammes, and tightening of the demerit points system considered.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the coming months, we will launch a new publicity campaign to raise awareness amongst all types of road users about road safety and the related measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: At the same time, we will further strengthen enforcement, starting first with drink-driving.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our current drink-driving standard is outdated and do not align with the latest scientific evidence and international norms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will lower the drink-driving limit, from the current 35 microgrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, to 15 microgrammes, aligning with jurisdictions, like Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To motivate all drivers to adhere closely to traffic rules, MHA is also considering tightening the demerit points system, including reducing the number of demerit points that can be accumulated before a driver is suspended and also increasing the suspension periods.

sections.label: Foreign vehicles traffic rule enforcement
sections.summary: Foreign-registered vehicles and motorcycles must comply with local traffic rules, and measures to strengthen enforcement against their violations are being studied.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Besides locally registered vehicles and motorcycles, we also require foreign-registered vehicles and motorcycles to comply with local traffic rules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We are studying several measures to strengthen enforcement against violations by such vehicles and motorcycles.

sections.label: Scam losses and cases 2025
sections.summary: Scam losses fell about $200 million or 18% from 2024, over $140 million was recovered, and 2025 saw over 37,000 cases and losses above $900 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Compared to 2024, scam losses decreased by about $200 million or 18%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The SPF's Anti-Scam Command also recovered more than $140 million in scam losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In 2025, there were more than 37,000 scam cases and total scam losses exceeded $900 million, which works out to roughly $100,000 every hour.

sections.label: GOIS cases and losses
sections.summary: GOIS cases more than doubled in 2025 to over 3,000, with the most and highest average loss per case at more than $72,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The number of GOIS cases reported in 2025 more than doubled to over 3,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Compared to other scam types, GOIS had the most and highest average amount lost per case at more than $72,000.

sections.label: OCHA online criminal content disruption
sections.summary: More than 150,000 instances of online criminal content, accounts and activities have been disrupted since OCHA's operationalisation in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: More than 150,000 instances of online criminal content, accounts and activities have been disrupted since OCHA's operationalisation in 2024.

sections.label: Scams on designated platforms decline
sections.summary: Scams on platforms of online service providers designated in 2024 declined by 36.5% in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Scams on platforms of online service providers designated in 2024 have declined by 36.5% in 2025.

sections.label: Approach used in scam cases
sections.summary: In 2025, this was the approach for more than 80% of the scam cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In 2025, this was the approach for more than 80% of the scam cases.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Command overseas takedowns
sections.summary: In 2025, the Anti-Scam Command and overseas law enforcement agencies took down 17 transnational scam syndicates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: In 2025, the close collaboration between the Anti-Scam Command and overseas law enforcement agencies resulted in the successful takedown of 17 transnational scam syndicates.

sections.label: ScamShield app downloads
sections.summary: The ScamShield mobile application now has 1.5 million downloads.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The ScamShield mobile application now has 1.5 million downloads.

sections.label: Helpline calls since September 2024
sections.summary: Since its September 2024 launch, the helpline has received more than 220,000 calls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Since the launch of the helpline in September 2024, it has received more than 220,000 calls.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses
sections.summary: Scam cases fell about 27% and losses dropped around $200 million, but total losses still exceeded $900 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Scam cases decreased by approximately 27% and losses from scams reduced by around $200 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The total amount of scam losses is still very high, exceeding $900 million.

sections.label: Crypto scam cases and losses
sections.summary: Crypto scam cases rose over 150% in 2025, with crypto losses about $182 million, or 20% of total scam losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: While overall scam cases decreased in 2025, cases involving crypto transactions increased by over 150%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Crypto losses accounted for about $182 million, or about 20% of total scam losses in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: On the other hand, the scam losses recovered through cryptocurrency only amounted to about 16% of scam losses.

sections.label: Tether, Ethereum, Bitcoin losses
sections.summary: Tether, Ethereum and Bitcoin account for about 92% of total crypto scam losses reported by victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In terms of specific cryptocurrencies that scam victims reported losing, Tether, Ethereum and Bitcoin account for about 92% of total crypto scam losses.

sections.label: CNB online drug trafficking measures
sections.summary: CNB employs measures to tackle online drug trafficking on virtual platforms, which offer no safe haven to offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
sentences.text: How is CNB dealing with drugs trade on virtual platforms, like e-commerce marketplaces and encrypted messaging apps?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, while the virtual platforms seem to provide anonymity to the drug offenders, they must know that there is no safe haven for them, because CNB employs a slew of measures or strategies to tackle online drug trafficking.

sections.label: Telegram drug orders detention order
sections.summary: A man used Telegram to receive orders and arrange drug exports to Singapore, and was issued a detention order under the CLTPA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, he was using Telegram to receive and collate orders, and then arrange for drugs to be exported to Singapore, where it would be received and distributed by his associate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So 22 September last year, he was issued a detention order under the Criminal Law Act (CLTPA) in view of his involvement in drug trafficking activities.

sections.label: ICA parcels referred to CNB
sections.summary: In 2025, ICA Air Cargo Command officers detected and referred 166 parcels to CNB for investigation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, in 2025, ICA Air Cargo Command officers detected and referred 166 parcels to CNB for investigation.

sections.label: Drug messages found to be scams
sections.summary: CNB found many WhatsApp or Telegram drug offers are scams where clients pay but receive no products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I have also received messages forwarded from fellow Members of the House, telling me that actually they have received such messages, peddling soft drugs, from their own residents, highlighting that this is a concern, especially if youths who tend to be more on social media receive such messages and are tempted that it is easy to get, seemingly affordable and anonymous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: But actually, when I forwarded it to our CNB colleagues for them to follow up, they came back to say that actually, for many of these text messages, be it on WhatsApp or Telegram, these are not really drug offers but actually it is a scam whereby potential clients, after making payment do not and will not actually receive the products that are promised to them.

sections.label: Alcohol limits and impairment studies
sections.summary: Alcohol limits enforced since 1985 are among the highest, and studies show impairment increases with consumption, even below current limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: To Ms Cassandra Lee's question, the alcohol limits that are currently enforced have been in place since 1985, and that is more than forty years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Now, Singapore is one of the jurisdictions with the highest alcohol limits, while the other jurisdictions have adopted stricter regimes with lower limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The studies have shown that the proportion of drivers exhibiting impairment, as well as the severity of impairment, increases progressively with alcohol consumption, and that impairment can happen at levels lower than our current prescribed limits.

sections.label: Mental health screening under-reporting concern
sections.summary: A question asks if self-reported questionnaires under-report mental health conditions among drug abusers and if closing this gap has value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: Second, given that the screening relies partly on self-reported questionnaires, is the Ministry concerned that the actual prevalence of mental health conditions among drug abusers may be significantly under-reported?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: Does the Ministry see value in closing this gap, so that we have a more complete picture of the mental health needs of all drug abusers in contact with the system, not just those in the prison or DRC in our fight to reduce recidivism?

sections.label: Data and National Healthcare link
sections.summary: Data collected includes survey and questionnaire data, and there is also a link to the National Healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And the data that we have is not only what we collect from survey and from questionnaire.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We also have a link to the National Healthcare system.

sections.label: Fujian gang recovery distribution
sections.summary: In some cases, such as the Fujian gang, recoveries may come from unidentifiable victims and it is not easy to know how the money will be distributed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: In some cases where the recoveries, for example, with the Fujian gang, maybe from victims who are unidentifiable, there is a large sum of money, it is not so easy to know how that money will be distributed.

sections.label: Road Traffic Penalty framework review
sections.summary: The Ministry is reviewing the Road Traffic Penalty framework and consulting unions on proportionate penalties, education and support for vocational drivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: As the Ministry reviews the Road Traffic Penalty framework, will the Ministry also consider how penalties can remain proportionate and whether there will be continued avenues for education and support, especially for our vocational drivers, taxi, private hire cars (PHC), bus captains, whose work exposure on the roads is significantly higher, so that road safety improvements can be achieved without unintended livelihood cost?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: If safety is compromised, then livelihoods and many other good things in life are going to be at risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We believe that the public will see our proposed for changes in this light, particularly our vocational drivers, because safer roads also mean a safer working environment for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Nonetheless, it is also very natural for road users to ask, "What do these proposed changes mean for me?" And it is in this spirit that we, with Ms Yeo Wan Ling's help, have been consulting the unions and we are very grateful for the opportunity to hear directly from vocational drivers, and we will be taking their perspectives fully into account.
